title: Descriptor-space k-nearest-neighbour rank member
spec: Quantile-transform each clipped full-RDKit descriptor column using the training-fold quantiles (map to a uniform distribution, then to standard normal), and drop constant columns. For each test molecule find its k=15 nearest training molecules by Euclidean distance in this scaled descriptor space, weighting neighbours by 1/(distance+1e-3), and take the weighted positive fraction as the score. Rank-normalise the score and add it as a third equal-weight rank member. Unlike the Tanimoto fingerprint kNN already tried, this neighbourhood is defined by physicochemical properties, which the descriptor results suggest carry most of the signal.

title: Remove near-constant fingerprint bits
spec: Before fitting, drop columns of the training fingerprint matrix whose frequency across training molecules is below 1% or above 99% (computed on training fold only), and apply the same column mask to the test matrix. Removing rare and near-universal bits reduces noise and speeds up the forest's split search.

title: Soft-label distillation from out-of-fold RF scores
spec: Within fit_predict, build soft targets for the training rows: take inner 5-fold, scaffold-grouped out-of-fold RF probabilities and mix them with the hard labels, t = 0.7 * y + 0.3 * oof_p. Fit the LightGBM member as a regressor (LGBMRegressor, objective='cross_entropy' with the soft targets in [0,1]) on the full matrix. Predict test scores as the LightGBM output. This regularizes the boosted trees against the label noise of borderline molecules. Keep the RF member and the rank blend unchanged.

title: LightGBM regularization via path smoothing and hessian floor
spec: Change the LightGBM member to LGBMClassifier(n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.04, num_leaves=15, max_bin=31, min_child_samples=20, min_child_weight=1.0, path_smooth=5.0, reg_lambda=2.0, colsample_bytree=0.3, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1). Path smoothing shrinks leaf values toward their parents and max_bin=31 coarsens the descriptor splits, both of which reduce overfitting to individual scaffold families. Leave the RF member and the rank blend unchanged.

title: Mixed-max-features RF ensemble
spec: Replace the single RandomForest with three forests of 200 trees each, trained with max_features set to 0.1, 0.3 and 0.6 (each with its own seed offset, random_state=seed+k). Average their predict_proba outputs, then feed that average into the existing rank blend in place of the single RF probability. Varying max_features mixes forests that favour different descriptor sets, and it is cheap because each forest is smaller than the incumbent. Keep the LightGBM member unchanged.

title: GBDT leaf embedding with a regularized logistic
spec: Fit the RF as usual and the LightGBM member as usual, but add a third member. Take the leaf index for each training and test row from the fitted LightGBM (booster.predict with pred_leaf=True). One-hot encode the leaf indices and fit an L2-regularized logistic regression (C=0.3, lbfgs, max_iter=2000, seeded) on the training one-hot matrix. Rank-average its test probabilities with the RF and LightGBM ranks as an equal third member. The leaves give nonlinear descriptor interactions, and the logistic step solves a different, smoother objective than boosting.

title: Feature-curriculum LightGBM via init_model
spec: Fit a first LightGBM booster for 150 rounds (learning_rate=0.1) using only the 11 physchem descriptors and the 2048-bit Morgan bits removed, so it learns coarse size and polarity trends. Continue training from that model with init_model on the full feature matrix for 400 more rounds at learning_rate=0.03, with colsample_bytree=0.3. This two-phase curriculum makes the boosting path start from low-capacity physchem structure before the fingerprints are added. Use lgb.train with the same seed. Keep the RF member and the rank blend unchanged.

title: Gaussian-process classifier on quantile-scaled descriptors
spec: Add a probabilistic non-tree model: quantile-transform the full cleaned descriptor matrix (as above), then reduce to the top 64 columns by mutual_info_classif on the training set (random_state=seed), and fit sklearn.gaussian_process.GaussianProcessClassifier with kernel ConstantKernel()*RBF(length_scale=np.ones(64)*5.0) and n_restarts_optimizer=0. Score test rows with predict_proba and rank-average the result into the blend at weight 1/3. The GP gives smooth, similarity-based probabilities in descriptor space that differ from tree splits and can help AUROC on the unseen-skeleton folds.

title: Firth-penalised logistic on spline-expanded descriptors
spec: Add a bias-reduced logistic model as a replacement for nothing: fit it as a separate member. Expand each clipped, quantile-scaled descriptor column with 4 natural cubic spline basis functions, then fit logistic regression by Newton iterations with Firth's modified score (the Jeffreys-prior penalty using the hat matrix diagonal), 25 iterations, ridge 1e-3 for stability. Rank-average its test probabilities with the RF and LightGBM ranks at weight 0.25 each, and the RF/LightGBM weights at 0.375 each.

title: Multi-task numpy MLP with auxiliary descriptor targets
spec: Replace the blend member set with one small fully connected network written in numpy (one or two hidden layers of 128 units, ReLU, Adam, weight decay 1e-3, about 200 epochs, batch 64, seeded). Its inputs are the quantile-clipped full descriptor matrix plus Morgan bits. Its outputs are the BBB label (sigmoid, cross-entropy) and, as auxiliary heads, standardized regression targets for MolWt, Crippen LogP, TPSA, and HBD/HBA counts (MSE, weight 0.3). Only the label head is used at prediction time. Rank-average its test probability with the existing RF and LightGBM members at equal weight.

title: Anti-clustering sample weights by local density
spec: Compute a per-training-molecule local density in standardized descriptor space (mean Euclidean distance to its 20 nearest training neighbours, using the training fold only). Set sample weight proportional to this distance, normalized to mean 1, so that molecules in dense clusters (often over-represented scaffold families) get less weight. Pass the weights to RandomForestClassifier.fit and LGBMClassifier.fit. Clip the weights to [0.2, 5] before normalizing.

title: Ring-topology composition features
spec: Append a small hand-built ring-topology vector to each molecule's features: number of ring systems (groups of fused or spiro-connected rings), size of the largest ring system in rings and in atoms, count of fused-ring bonds, count of bridgehead atoms, histogram of ring sizes (3 to 8 and larger), number of aromatic heterocycles, and number of non-aromatic rings containing N or O. Compute from mol.GetRingInfo() and simple SMARTS checks. These go alongside the existing descriptors and the 2048-bit Morgan vector, with no other change.

title: Generic-scaffold target encoding
spec: Compute each molecule's generic Murcko scaffold (all atoms set to carbon, all bonds set to single) and map it to a smoothed training-label mean: (sum of y + 5 * global_mean) / (n + 5). Use out-of-fold encoding inside fit_predict (5 inner folds grouped by scaffold) so training rows never see their own label. Unseen generic scaffolds get the global mean. Append the encoded value, plus the scaffold's training count, as two columns to X_train and X_test. Leave the RF and LightGBM members and the rank blend unchanged.

title: Per-atom Crippen and TPSA contribution histograms
spec: Add a new block of features computed per molecule: for each heavy atom, take its Crippen logP atom contribution (rdMolDescriptors._CalcCrippenContribs) and its Ertl-style TPSA contribution (per-atom polar surface area from rdMolDescriptors._CalcTPSAContribs). Bin each contribution list into a fixed 10-bin histogram over a fixed range, and also record the sum of positive and sum of negative contributions for each. Concatenate these roughly 24 numbers to the existing feature matrix for both RF and LightGBM. Fixed bin edges are used so train and test features are consistent.

title: Gaussian-jitter augmentation of descriptors
spec: Before fitting the LightGBM member, make 3 noisy copies of the training matrix. Each copy adds N(0, 0.05 * IQR_j) noise to every descriptor column j (IQR computed on the training data, fingerprint bits left unchanged), using a numpy RandomState seeded from the seed argument. Stack the original and the copies (4x rows) with labels repeated, and fit LGBMClassifier with the same hyperparameters but min_child_samples raised to 40 to offset the duplicated rows. The augmentation smooths split thresholds over the descriptor space and should help generalisation to new scaffolds.

title: Pairwise crosses of top descriptors
spec: After building the existing descriptor block, pick the 12 full-descList columns with the highest absolute point-biserial correlation to the training labels (computed inside fit_predict on the training fold only). Append all pairwise products of those 12 clipped, standardized columns (66 columns) and the pairwise differences of the 4 most label-correlated columns, then feed the enlarged matrix to both the RandomForest and LightGBM members. Keep everything else unchanged.

title: Explainable boosting-style additive model
spec: Add an additive shape-function member in numpy. Bin each clipped full-descList column into 16 quantile bins using training-fold edges. Cycle over features for 40 rounds: in each round, for each feature fit a one-dimensional shrunk logit-leaf update on the current residual (learning rate 0.1) and accumulate per-bin scores. Predict with the sum of per-feature bin scores passed through a sigmoid. Blend its rank with the RF and LightGBM ranks equally. Use the seed only to break ties in the feature order.

title: Truncated SVD of the fingerprint as dense appended features
spec: Inside fit_predict, fit sklearn TruncatedSVD (n_components=64, random_state=seed) on the Morgan bit matrix of the training fold only, then transform both train and test fingerprints. Append the 64 SVD scores to the existing feature matrix (fingerprint bits, clipped descriptors) for the RF and LightGBM members. Because the SVD sees only training rows and is unsupervised, there is no label leakage. The dense low-rank summaries give each tree a set of broadly informative axes where single bits are sparse.

title: Ionization-corrected logD surrogate
spec: Add a continuous ionization-aware lipophilicity feature. Use SMARTS patterns for carboxylic acid (pKa about 4.5), tetrazole (about 5), phenol (about 10), aliphatic tertiary amine (about 9.5), secondary amine (about 10), and amidine or guanidine (about 12). For each molecule compute the Henderson-Hasselbalch correction at pH 7.4 for each matched group (log10(1 + 10^(pH-pKa)) for acids and log10(1 + 10^(pKa-pH)) for bases), sum them, and append logD = Crippen LogP minus the summed correction, plus the summed correction itself. Clip with the existing 1st/99th percentile rule.

title: Conformer-averaged 3D shape descriptors
spec: Replace the single-conformer shape block with an average over 5 ETKDG conformers per molecule. Embed with rdDistGeom.ETKDGv3 using randomSeed=seed, MMFF-optimize, and compute PMI1-3, NPR1-2, PBF and radius of gyration for each conformer. Append the mean and standard deviation over conformers (16 columns) to the existing feature matrix. Skip molecules that fail embedding by setting their 3D features to zero. Keep everything else unchanged.

title: Mahalanobis out-of-distribution feature
spec: Inside fit_predict, standardize the 11-column physchem block and the 40 most variable clipped full-descList columns using training-fold statistics. Fit sklearn MinCovDet with random_state=seed on the training rows, and compute each molecule's squared Mahalanobis distance from the robust centre. Append this single distance as a feature to both the RandomForest and LightGBM matrices. The feature measures how atypical a molecule is, which may relate to penetration on unseen scaffolds.

title: Generative Gaussian classifier on PCA-whitened descriptors
spec: Standardise the clipped full-RDKit descriptor matrix on the training fold and reduce it to 20 principal components. Fit one multivariate Gaussian per class (mean and covariance with a ridge term 1e-2 added to the diagonal) on the training rows, and compute the test log-likelihood ratio log p(x|y=1) + log prior ratio. Convert that score to a probability with a sigmoid of its centred value, then rank-normalise it and add it as a third member with equal weight alongside the existing RF and LightGBM ranks. This is a deliberately different generative model that makes a Gaussian assumption about the descriptor distribution.

title: Subsample rows per tree (smaller bootstrap)
spec: Set RandomForestClassifier max_samples=0.6 with bootstrap=True and increase n_estimators to 600. Smaller bootstrap samples decorrelate trees more strongly, which often improves ranking quality (AUROC) on noisy, small datasets while keeping the forest size reasonable.

title: Test-neighbourhood smoothing of predictions
spec: After the blended rank score is computed for the test molecules, build the Tanimoto similarity matrix among test molecules only (Morgan bit fingerprints). For each test molecule keep its 5 nearest test neighbours with similarity above 0.3, and replace its score with 0.7 times its own score plus 0.3 times the mean score of those neighbours. If no neighbour passes the threshold, keep the original score. Re-rank the result with scaled_rank. This exploits local structure within the held-out fold, which is a different use of test data from the previously tried label spreading.

title: Descriptor-manifold Laplacian-regularised logistic
spec: Use transduction over train and test together. Standardize the clipped full descriptors using the training fold statistics. Build a symmetric k-nearest-neighbour graph (k=10, Euclidean distance on the standardized descriptors) over all training plus test molecules, and form its normalized Laplacian L. Fit a logistic model f = X w by minimizing the logistic loss on labelled training rows plus lambda * f^T L f with lambda about 1.0, using L-BFGS from scipy.optimize with the gradient written out. Test predictions are the sigmoid of f on test rows. Add this as a third rank-averaged member with equal weight. This smooths scores along the descriptor manifold, a different mechanism from the Tanimoto label spreading that was tried earlier.

title: RuleFit-style rule ensemble
spec: Inside fit_predict, fit a shallow LightGBM (about 100 trees, num_leaves 4, learning_rate 0.1, seeded) on the clipped full descriptor matrix plus the Morgan bits. Convert every leaf of every tree into a binary rule feature: 1 if a sample falls into that leaf, else 0. Stack these leaf indicators with the standardized clipped descriptors and fit an L1-penalised logistic regression (saga or liblinear, C tuned to about 0.1 to 0.3 by a fixed choice, not by test data). Return its predicted probability for the test molecules as one more rank-averaged member alongside the existing RF and LightGBM blend, with equal weight.

title: Naive Bayes member on binarised descriptors and fingerprint bits
spec: Add a diverse, very cheap member. Binarise each descriptor column into 8 quantile bins using training-set edges, one-hot encode the bins, and concatenate with the 2048 Morgan bits. Fit sklearn BernoulliNB(alpha=1.0) on this binary matrix. Blend its test-set rank score into the existing rank average with weight 0.2, renormalising the other two weights to 0.4 each. Naive Bayes makes strongly different errors from trees and is nearly free to fit, so it may add ensemble diversity.

title: Degree-2 polynomial L1 logistic on top descriptors
spec: Select the 40 clipped full descriptors with the highest absolute Spearman correlation to the training labels (computed on the training fold only). Standardize them and expand to all pairwise products and squares, giving about 860 columns. Fit a logistic regression with an L1 penalty (liblinear, C set to 0.05 a priori) on these columns. Use its probabilities as a third rank-averaged member next to the RF and LightGBM blend, with equal weight. The aim is a sparse, explicit interaction model of physicochemical properties.

title: Small numpy message-passing graph network
spec: Replace the RF+LightGBM blend with a from-scratch graph neural network written in numpy. Atom features: element one-hot for the common elements, degree, total H count, formal charge, aromaticity, and in-ring flag. Use 3 rounds of message passing: each atom sums its neighbours' hidden vectors, then applies a shared dense layer with ReLU and a residual connection. Use hidden size 64. Global sum pooling and mean pooling are concatenated with the standardised, clipped RDKit descriptors, then a dense sigmoid output. Train with full-batch or minibatch Adam, learning rate 1e-3, weight decay 1e-4, about 150 epochs, with the seed controlling initialisation. Average 3 seeds and rank-blend the output 50/50 with the existing LightGBM member. Keep the total fit time per fold under 30 seconds.

title: Two-view co-training with fingerprint and descriptor models
spec: Train two separate models on the training data: a fingerprint-only model (LightGBM on the 2048 Morgan bits) and a descriptor-only model (RF on the clipped full descriptor list). For each round, use each model to score the test molecules and take the 10% most confident test predictions from each (highest and lowest rank) as pseudo-labels for the other view. Add those pseudo-labelled test rows to the other view's training set and refit. Run 2 rounds, then return the rank average of the final two models' test predictions. The procedure is transductive and uses only the test SMILES, not the test labels.

title: LightGBM with linear leaves on descriptors
spec: Replace the current LGBMClassifier member with a LightGBM model that has linear_tree=True (piecewise-linear leaf models, linear_lambda=1.0), trained on the same matrix of Morgan bits plus clipped descriptors. Keep num_leaves at 15 and colsample_bytree at 0.3, and use min_child_samples=20 so the linear fits are stable. Keep the RF and the rank blend unchanged. This gives the boosting member smooth within-leaf trends in the physicochemical columns, without adding new features.

title: Unfolded radius-3 count fingerprint
spec: Replace the radius-2 2048-bit Morgan bit vector with a radius-3 Morgan count vector folded to 4096 bins, computed with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy. Keep the descriptor block and the existing RF and LightGBM members unchanged, and let the forest use the larger input. Only the fingerprint generator changes.

title: Group-wise ridge penalties over descriptor families
spec: Split the columns into three groups: Morgan bits, the 11 physchem columns, and the remaining full RDKit descriptors. Fit an L2 logistic regression on the clipped and standardized matrix where each group has its own penalty scale multiplying a shared alpha, implemented by dividing that group's standardized columns by its penalty scale before fitting. Choose the three scales from {0.3, 1, 3} by a 3-fold inner scaffold-grouped CV on the training fold. Add this model's scaled rank as a third equal-weight member of the blend.

title: Small grid of LightGBM leaf and feature-fraction settings
spec: Replace the single LightGBM member with a 4-model grid over min_child_samples in {10, 40} and colsample_bytree in {0.1, 0.3}, each at 300 rounds and learning_rate 0.05. Fit all four on the same matrix with seeds from the seed argument, scale each model's test probabilities by rank, and average the four rank vectors into one LightGBM member for the blend. This tests whether the descriptor-dominated matrix prefers a different leaf size or feature sampling than the current defaults.

title: Rank-median over several forest seeds
spec: Instead of one RandomForestClassifier, train five forests on the same matrix with seeds derived from the seed argument (seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4), each with 200 trees. For each test molecule, take the median of the five scaled-rank scores rather than the mean. Keep the LightGBM member and the 50/50 rank blend as they are. The median is used so that one unusually scored forest does not dominate the ranking.

title: Prototype-distance features from training-fold k-means
spec: Inside fit_predict, standardize the clipped full-descriptor block on the training fold and run k-means (k=30, seeded, n_init=3) on it. Append to each molecule its Euclidean distance to all 30 centroids, log-transformed, as 30 extra columns, computed identically for train and test using the training-fold centroids. Feed the enlarged matrix to the existing RF and LightGBM members. This gives the trees a coarse, learned chemotype map without any labels.

title: Early-stopped boosting with inner validation
spec: Inside fit_predict, hold out a stratified 15% of the training fold for validation. Train an LGBMClassifier with up to 1000 rounds (learning_rate 0.03, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.8) and early_stopping_rounds=50 on the validation split, then refit on the full training fold using the best iteration count (scaled by 1.1). Automatic round selection avoids a hand-picked and possibly overfit tree count.

title: Two-pass hard-example reweighting
spec: Train a first pass of the existing RF and LightGBM using the normal training data. Compute out-of-fold predictions on the training molecules with a 5-fold GroupKFold grouped by scaffold, using the seed. Identify training molecules whose out-of-fold rank is on the wrong side of the label, for example positives with a low score or negatives with a high score, and set their sample weight to 2.0 while leaving the rest at 1.0. Refit both models with these sample weights and blend the new predictions with the same rank-average. This targets the hard, possibly noisy molecules without removing them.

title: Larger forest with sqrt feature sampling
spec: Raise the RandomForestClassifier to n_estimators=1000 and switch max_features from 0.3 to 'sqrt', keeping min_samples_leaf=1 and random_state=seed. More trees reduce the variance of the forest's rank scores, and sqrt feature sampling decorrelates trees on the wide full-descriptor matrix. Runtime should stay well under the 10-minute job limit because the features and LightGBM member are unchanged.

title: Shallower-leaf RF with a depth cap
spec: Keep the 300-tree forest on the existing features and set min_samples_leaf=3 and max_depth=18 in RandomForestClassifier. The aim is smoother class-1 probabilities that rank better across unseen scaffolds, and this is a regularization test on forest complexity. Leave the LightGBM member and the rank blend unchanged, so the only change is the forest constructor arguments.

title: RBF-SVC member on quantile-scaled descriptors
spec: Add a kernel member that works on continuous descriptors instead of fingerprints. Fit a QuantileTransformer (normal output) on the training-fold clipped full descriptor matrix, then fit sklearn SVC(kernel='rbf', C=1.0, gamma='scale', probability=True, random_state=seed) on it. Use its test probabilities as the replacement for the LightGBM member's score in the rank blend, so the blend stays two-member RF plus SVC. Standardize with the training-fold statistics only.

title: Stability selection over scaffold bootstraps
spec: Inside fit_predict, draw 20 scaffold-level bootstrap samples of the training fold (resample Murcko scaffold groups with replacement). On each sample, fit a quick LightGBM on the full concatenated matrix and record which columns have nonzero gain importance. Keep only columns selected in at least 60% of the 20 draws, then fit the existing RandomForest and LightGBM on that reduced matrix. Use the seed argument for all draws. Fall back to the full matrix if fewer than 20 columns survive.

title: MQN count descriptor block
spec: Append the 42 MQN (molecular quantum numbers) counts from rdMolDescriptors.MQNs_(mol) to each molecule's feature vector, next to the existing Morgan bits and full descList columns. Apply the same 1st/99th-percentile clipping that the script already uses for descriptors, fitted on the training fold only. Nothing else changes. MQN is not part of Descriptors.descList, so this adds integer count information the current feature set lacks.

title: Pairwise difference ranker on descriptors
spec: Train a pairwise ranker that targets AUROC directly. Sample about 150k random pairs (i, j) from the training fold with y_i != y_j, using a seed-driven generator. For each pair, build the feature x_i - x_j on the clipped, standardized full-descriptor matrix and label it 1 if y_i = 1 and y_j = 0, otherwise 0 (with random sign flipping to keep the label balanced). Fit a LogisticRegression without intercept (C=1.0) or a LightGBM with 200 rounds on these difference rows. For a test molecule, the score is the mean over a fixed set of 200 training anchors of the predicted pairwise probability of its difference against each anchor, mapped to a rank. Use this rank as an extra member in the existing blend, or use it alone to compare. The design rewards correct ordering rather than calibrated probabilities.

title: Fingerprint-cluster target encoding
spec: Run k-means (k=40, seeded, on the 2048 Morgan bits as floats) on the training fingerprints. For each cluster, compute a smoothed out-of-fold label mean (5 inner folds grouped by scaffold, same smoothing as a prior of 5 pseudo-counts). Assign each test molecule to its nearest training centroid and use that cluster's mean as one extra column. Append the cluster mean and the cluster size as two columns to both X_train and X_test. Keep the rest of the pipeline the same.

title: Out-of-fold Fisher LDA projection feature
spec: Before fitting the RF and LightGBM, compute one supervised feature: a Fisher linear discriminant direction on the clipped full-descriptor matrix, standardized and with shrinkage covariance (Ledoit-Wolf or covariance + 0.1*I). To avoid leakage, produce the training-row values out-of-fold with an inner 5-fold stratified split on the training fold (each row scored by a discriminant fit without it), and produce test-row values from a discriminant fit on the full training fold. Append the single scalar projection as one extra column to both matrices. The idea is a linear, class-aware summary that trees can split on directly.

title: L1 logistic regression on Morgan bits and descriptors replaces the forest
spec: Replace the RandomForest member with a sparse linear model. Build the input from the binary 2048-bit Morgan vector plus the standardized clipped full descriptor matrix (z-score using training-fold mean and std, with zero-variance columns dropped). Fit LogisticRegression(penalty='l1', solver='liblinear', C=0.1, max_iter=2000, random_state=seed) and keep the LightGBM member and the rank blend exactly as they are. This tests whether a linear, sparsity-driven model on the same inputs generalises better across unseen scaffolds than the forest. It is a bold model-family swap, so the blend weights should stay equal.

title: Random-forest leaf embedding with a regularized logistic head
spec: Fit the existing RandomForest on the training fold as now. Use rf.apply(X) to get the leaf index of every training and test row in every tree. One-hot encode the leaf indices with sklearn OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore') fitted on the training leaves, giving a very sparse binary matrix with one active column per tree. Train a LogisticRegression (C=0.05, max_iter=2000, seeded) on that embedding and use its test probability as a third signal in place of the LightGBM member, so the blend becomes RF rank plus embedding-logistic rank. This is a bolder change that turns the forest into a learned sparse representation and lets a linear model reweight which tree leaves matter.

title: Stereo and salt-fragment count features
spec: Append a small block of counts that the descriptor list does not cover: number of stereocentres (Chem.FindMolChiralCenters with includeUnassigned=True), number of double bonds with E/Z stereo, count of unassigned stereo elements, number of disconnected fragments in the input SMILES (salt or counterion flag), and the heavy-atom count of the smallest fragment. Compute them in featurize/full_descriptors alongside the existing columns, and pass them through the same percentile clipping before concatenation. No other change.

title: Descriptor-dominant features with a smaller Morgan radius-1 block
spec: Change the fingerprint part of featurize to radius 1 with 512 bits (the N_BITS and RADIUS settings) while keeping the full descList block exactly as now. Rationale: the notes show descriptors drive the gain, and a 2048-bit fingerprint dilutes feature sampling for the RF (max_features=0.3) and LightGBM (colsample_bytree=0.3). Keep the blend unchanged. Only the fingerprint width and radius change, so a single run should show whether the bit block is hurting the descriptor signal.

title: Genetic-programming feature synthesis on physchem columns
spec: Inside fit_predict, before the RF and LightGBM fit, run a small seeded genetic-programming search over arithmetic expressions of the 11 physchem descriptors (operators +, -, *, safe division, log1p, square, min, max; depth at most 3). Population 200, 15 generations, fitness = AUROC of a depth-limited 3-tree decision stump ensemble on a stratified inner split of the training fold. Keep the top 20 expressions by inner-validation AUROC and append them as extra columns to both train and test matrices, computed from the same clipped descriptor percentiles. Everything else is unchanged.

title: Gaussian-jitter augmentation of descriptor rows
spec: Augment the training descriptor matrix for the LightGBM member only. Make 3 noisy copies of each training row, adding independent Gaussian noise to each standardised descriptor column with standard deviation 0.05 (after quantile scaling fitted on training data). Concatenate the copies with the original labels and fit LightGBM with the same hyperparameters. The RF stays on the unaugmented features. Smoothing the decision function in descriptor space is a regulariser aimed at the cross-scaffold generalisation gap.

title: Label-noise filtering before fitting
spec: Before fitting the final models, run a 5-fold cross-validated RF on the training set using the same features. Mark as suspicious any training molecule whose out-of-fold predicted probability for its own label is below 0.1. Drop those rows (at most 10 percent of training data, keep the 10 percent with lowest own-label probability at most) and fit the RF and LightGBM blend on the remaining rows. The benchmark's BBB labels are noisy, so removing confidently contradicted examples may sharpen the decision boundary on unseen skeletons.

title: Cap tree depth in the forest
spec: Set max_depth=12 in RandomForestClassifier, keeping the other settings. Limiting depth controls memorization of individual molecules and scaffolds, which should help generalization across unseen Murcko scaffolds in this grouped evaluation.

title: Gasteiger partial-charge statistics on polar atoms
spec: Compute Gasteiger partial charges with rdkit.Chem.rdPartialCharges.ComputeGasteigerCharges(mol) once per molecule. From the per-atom charges, build 8 numbers: max and min charge over all atoms, sum of absolute charges, and for heteroatoms (N or O) the max, min, mean and count of charges, plus the count of atoms with |charge| > 0.2. Replace NaN and inf with 0, clip to the train-fold 1st/99th percentiles, and append to the feature matrix. Model and blend stay the same. This adds an electrostatic view of polarity that the existing TPSA and HBD/HBA counts only approximate.

title: Node-level feature subsampling in LightGBM
spec: In the LightGBM member, set feature_fraction=1.0 and feature_fraction_bynode=0.2 (replacing colsample_bytree=0.3), keeping num_leaves=15, learning_rate=0.05 and 300 estimators. Node-level sampling decorrelates splits within a tree rather than across the whole tree, which is a different regularizer from the per-tree column sample already used. Keep the RF and the rank blend unchanged.

title: Gradient-sampled LightGBM with per-tree row subsampling by scaffold
spec: Before fitting the LightGBM member, sample 80% of the training scaffolds (Murcko, generic-form not required) per boosting replicate and train 5 LightGBMs of 300 trees each on those row subsets, using bagging_fraction=1.0 within each replicate. Average the 5 rank scores as the LightGBM component. This differs from earlier scaffold-bootstrap bagging in that the subsets are drawn without replacement, so no duplicated rows appear. Keep the RF member and the rank blend unchanged.

title: EState fingerprint and EState index block
spec: Add two dense blocks per molecule, computed with rdkit.Chem.EState.Fingerprinter.FingerprintMol(mol): the 79-bin EState-count fingerprint (fp[0]) and the 79-value EState index vector (fp[1]). Concatenate them to the feature matrix after the existing descriptors, then apply the same train-fold 1st/99th percentile clipping used for the descriptors. Leave the model settings unchanged. EState indices encode electronic and topological environment of each atom type, which Morgan bits do not capture well.
